scheme_name: Agriculture And Processed Foods Export Promotion Scheme Of APEDA For The 15th Finance Commission Cycle (2021-22 To 2025-26)
description:
The Agriculture and Processed Foods Export Promotion Scheme is an initiative by the Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA). 

This scheme was launched to enhance the export of agricultural and processed food products from India. 

The scheme is part of the broader strategy to increase India's share in global agricultural exports. 

The 15th Finance Commission cycle covers the period from 2021-22 to 2025-26. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to promote the export of agricultural and processed food products. 

The scheme aims to increase the export of these products by 20% annually. 

The targeted export value is set to reach approximately USD 60 billion by the end of the 15th Finance Commission cycle. 

The scheme focuses on various products including fruits, vegetables, cereals, and processed foods. 

Specific benefits under this scheme include financial assistance for marketing and promotion of products. 

APEDA provides assistance of up to 50% of the total cost incurred for marketing activities. 

The maximum financial assistance can go up to INR 50 lakhs for individual exporters. 

For groups of exporters or cooperatives, the assistance can be up to INR 1 crore. 

Eligibility for the scheme includes exporters who are registered with APEDA. 

Exporters must have a valid Importer Exporter Code (IEC) issued by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT). 

The scheme is also open to cooperatives and producer organizations involved in the export of agricultural products. 

To apply for the scheme, exporters must submit an application to APEDA. 

The application must include details of the products intended for export. 

Exporters must also provide a marketing plan outlining the strategies to be employed. 

Required documents include a copy of the IEC, GST registration, and a bank account statement. 

The application process is conducted online through the APEDA website. 

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by APEDA officials. 

If approved, financial assistance is disbursed in installments based on the marketing activities undertaken. 

The scheme also encourages the establishment of quality control measures. 

Exporters are required to adhere to the quality standards set by APEDA. 

This includes obtaining necessary certifications such as FSSAI and ISO certifications. 

The timeline for the disbursement of funds is typically within 30 days of approval. 

APEDA conducts regular monitoring and evaluation of the scheme. 

This includes assessing the impact of the financial assistance on export performance. 

The scheme also aims to enhance the capacity of exporters through training programs. 

Training sessions are conducted on best practices in export marketing and quality control. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA). 

APEDA operates under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India. 

The contact details for APEDA can be found on their official website. 

The scheme is part of the government's larger initiative to double farmers' income by 2022. 

It aligns with the goals set forth in the National Policy on Agriculture. 

The policy emphasizes the importance of increasing agricultural productivity and enhancing farmers' income. 

The scheme also addresses the need for diversification of agricultural exports. 

By promoting processed foods, the scheme aims to reduce post-harvest losses. 

It encourages the use of modern technology in food processing and packaging. 

The scheme has provisions for supporting research and development in agricultural exports. 

APEDA collaborates with various research institutions to enhance product quality. 

The scheme also promotes participation in international trade fairs and exhibitions. 

This provides exporters with a platform to showcase their products globally. 

The government has allocated a budget of INR 2,000 crores for the 15th Finance Commission cycle. 

This budget is aimed at supporting various initiatives under the Agriculture and Processed Foods Export Promotion Scheme. 

The scheme also includes provisions for developing infrastructure for food processing. 

This includes setting up cold storage facilities and logistics support for exporters. 

The government encourages public-private partnerships to enhance export capabilities. 

The scheme is expected to create job opportunities in the agricultural sector. 

It aims to empower farmers by providing them with better market access. 

The scheme also focuses on promoting organic and sustainable farming practices. 

By doing so, it aims to enhance the global competitiveness of Indian agricultural products. 

The initiative is expected to have a significant impact on rural development. 

It will contribute to the overall economic growth of the country. 

The scheme is regularly updated to incorporate feedback from stakeholders. 

This ensures that it remains relevant to the changing dynamics of global trade. 

APEDA also provides a platform for resolving issues faced by exporters. 

This includes addressing challenges related to quality standards and market access. 

The Agriculture and Processed Foods Export Promotion Scheme is a vital component of India's export strategy. 

It plays a crucial role in enhancing the country's agricultural export potential. 

The scheme is designed to be inclusive and supports small and marginal farmers. 

By facilitating access to international markets, it aims to improve livelihoods. 

The government is committed to ensuring transparency and accountability in the implementation of the scheme. 

Regular audits and assessments are conducted to monitor the utilization of funds. 

The scheme is expected to contribute significantly to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals. 

It aligns with the goal of promoting sustainable agriculture and food security. 

Overall, the Agriculture and Processed Foods Export Promotion Scheme is a comprehensive initiative. 

It addresses multiple facets of agricultural export promotion in India. 

Through this scheme, the government aims to create a robust ecosystem for agricultural exports. 

This will ultimately benefit farmers and contribute to the nation's economic development.
